name: Jean-Jacques Rousseau
role: Genevan philosopher of popular sovereignty and the general will (1712-1778)
summary: Rousseau held that legitimate authority rests only on the consent of citizens who make the laws themselves as a sovereign people, with government a subordinate agent and representation of sovereignty rejected. He favoured small republics of modest equality and civic virtue, a civil religion, public education and citizen militias, and condemned luxury, hereditary rule and the corrupting effects of the arts and sciences. He also held that women should be subordinate to men within the family and excluded from public life.
